author: David Reed
summary: chg-26 repairs a false positive chg-25 put into the repo's strictest assertion. GC-018 forbade 'PD-L1 TPS', a bare criterion NAME. That worked while a JUDGE read the list, since a judge tells 'PD-L1 TPS: NOT documented' from 'PD-L1 TPS is 62%'. chg-25 moved the check to a string matcher, which cannot, so changing the READER redefined the keyword: a correct rationale listing what the notes omit failed the zero-tolerance gate on 1 of 6 runs. Rule: forbid assertions, never criterion names.

changes.description: Remove the bare criterion name 'PD-L1 TPS' from GC-018's reasoning_must_not_include, leaving its two assertion-shaped traps ('EGFR negative', 'test results confirm') in place. Add describe_sparse_trap_violation() so the zero-tolerance assertion names which arm fired (judge Tier 3 vs deterministic Tier 1) and on which keyword. Record the authoring rule in docs/CASE_AUTHORING_GUIDE.md and correct two stale trap-list examples there.
changes.failure_pattern: The repo's zero-tolerance anti-hallucination gate failed the build on correct agent behaviour, reporting 'FABRICATION DETECTED' for a rationale that fabricated nothing. Because the gate is nondeterministic and now a required CI status check, the failure was also unreproducible on demand and unattributed: the assertion named the case but not which of its two ORed signals fired.
changes.root_cause: A category error inherited from chg-25, not a matcher bug. GC-018's reasoning_must_not_include entries were authored for an LLM judge, which reads them semantically. 'PD-L1 TPS' names a criterion and asserts nothing, so a judge correctly reads 'PD-L1 TPS status: NOT documented' as the opposite of a fabrication. chg-25 moved the check into whole-word string matching -- correct for anything lexical, but it silently redefined every keyword whose meaning depended on a reader that understood negation. GC-018 makes the collision unavoidable rather than unlucky: its reasoning_must_include demands 'PD-L1', and its own guidelines_context hands the agent the phrase verbatim ('PD-L1 TPS >= 50% confirmed by validated assay'), while a sparse-notes case invites precisely the enumeration of missing items that must name them.
predicted_fixes: A rationale reporting the PD-L1 result as undocumented no longer registers a Tier 1 forbidden-keyword hit on GC-018, so it no longer trips the zero-tolerance gate. Deterministic and provable without live calls: test_naming_an_absent_criterion_is_not_a_fabrication pins the verbatim failing rationale and fails against the pre-chg-26 case data.

The gate is not blunted by the removal. An invented lab value still trips a deterministic trap even when the judge is lenient, via the surviving assertion-shaped keywords -- pinned by test_gc_018_still_catches_an_asserted_lab_value.

Any future sparse-trap failure is diagnosable from CI output alone, because the assertion now names the arm that fired and the exact keyword. This is a diagnosability claim, not a correctness one, and it is the reason the residual flake below is now investigable instead of requiring a fresh live run.
risk_cases: UNRESOLVED, and stated rather than hidden: the live gate still failed 1 of 3 runs AFTER this fix, and that occurrence is unattributed -- the failure predates the attribution message, so there is no record of whether the judge arm or a surviving keyword fired. Eight further probe trials (4 each on GC-018 and GC-019, both arms captured) came back clean, which narrows the rate but explains nothing. The most plausible remaining source is the judge's fabrication_detected boolean, which chg-25's own risk_cases already flagged as able to move without the system moving. Do not read this change as 'the gate is now stable'.

The surviving traps are assertion-shaped but not negation-proof. 'no test results confirm eligibility' and 'no EGFR negative result was provided' would both trip Tier 1 while being correct. Not observed in 8 probe trials, but the same class as the defect fixed here, and it is the first thing to check when the gate next flakes.

Removing the keyword narrows deterministic coverage: a fabricated PD-L1 value phrased without an assertion trap ('PD-L1 TPS 62%') is now caught only by the judge arm. Accepted deliberately -- a value-bearing pattern ('PD-L1 TPS of') catches one phrasing and misses 'is 62%' and bare '62%', and a trap that looks deterministic while being partial is the failure mode chg-25 existed to remove.

Scope is one keyword on one case, because two attempts at a structural rule for finding others died against the data: 'a forbidden keyword that contains a required keyword' flags 12 cases including GC-019, which does not have this defect; a bare-noun-phrase heuristic flags 154 traps and misses this one. The distinction is semantic and stays authoring judgment, which is why the durable artifact is a guide rule rather than a dataset-integrity check.

PRE-EXISTING, carried forward from chg-25 and still open: GC-101/102/103 are duplicated across adult_complexity_cases.py and oncology_breadth_cases.py (109 case-id occurrences, 106 unique). Counters keyed by case_id remain ambiguous for those three. Needs its own change.
changes.why_this_component: GC-018 is the case behind test_zero_fabrications_on_sparse_cases, the repo's single most safety-critical assertion and a required status check on main. A gate that fails on correct behaviour is worse than one that is merely noisy: it trains readers to re-run until green, which is exactly how a real fabrication would eventually be waved through. Fixing the keyword restores the gate's meaning; the attribution message restores its usability.
changes.rollback_plan: Restore 'PD-L1 TPS' to GC-018's reasoning_must_not_include and revert the two tests that pin its absence. The attribution helper and the authoring-guide rule are independent and should be kept regardless -- neither changes what the gate decides, only what it reports. No src/ file is touched and there is no schema change, so the runtime is unaffected.

baseline.claim: Before chg-26, GC-018's reasoning_must_not_include contained 'PD-L1 TPS', and a correct rationale reporting that criterion as undocumented produced a Tier 1 forbidden-keyword hit, tripping the zero-tolerance gate with no fabrication present.
baseline.verified_by: Six live agent runs on GC-018 at HEAD 2c3eaa7, each scored with check_reasoning_constraints(); plus the make test-clinical failure at the same HEAD.
baseline.result: 1 of 6 runs produced a Tier 1 hit on 'PD-L1 TPS', verbatim: '**PD-L1 TPS status:** NOT documented. No assay result, no percentage, no date.' The clinical gate failed with 'FABRICATION DETECTED -- ZERO TOLERANCE VIOLATION Cases with a confirmed violation: [GC-018]'. Judge fabrication_detected was False in the same runs, confirming the Tier 1 arm as the source.

verified_fixes: The deterministic counters are separated and independently reported, as predicted. The live run at HEAD 2c3eaa7 printed constraint violations, ungrounded citations and outcome mismatches as distinct lines with distinct case lists, replacing the single conflated 'hallucinations' counter.

The whole-word correction holds on the dataset it was measured against: GC-046 and GC-048 no longer appear in the forbidden-present list ('coverage', 'average'), while GC-028 still does -- now recorded as a keyword constraint rather than a hallucination.
Ungrounded citations reported 0 across 39 cases, and the eval grounding demonstrably reuses the runtime detector rather than a copy.

The AND-ed sparse-trap gate does close the gap it was built for: a lenient judge plus an invented lab value is still caught by the deterministic arm alone (test_gc_018_still_catches_an_asserted_lab_value, carried forward at chg-26).
missed_fixes: The third predicted fix -- ORing a Tier 1 trap-keyword hit into the sparse-fabrication gate -- was implemented as designed but the design was wrong for two of GC-018's three keywords. The trap lists were authored for a judge and encode semantic claims; read by a string matcher, 'PD-L1 TPS' matches correct rationales that report the criterion as ABSENT. Result: the repo's strictest assertion began failing builds on correct behaviour, measured at 1 of 6 live runs. Fixed by chg-26.

F3's stated premise -- 'a signal a function already computes exactly' -- did not hold for this keyword. The function computes phrase presence exactly; phrase presence is not the fabrication signal. This is P-013 recurring inside the very change that was written to honour it: the claim about what the deterministic check would mean was reasoned about, not measured against agent output.

The judge arm remains able to move without the system moving, as chg-25 itself predicted. A live gate failure 1 of 3 runs after chg-26 is unattributed and most plausibly this. chg-26 adds the attribution needed to confirm it next time.
verdicts.notes: Kept and refined rather than rolled back: the three-tier separation is right, the instability it was built to fix is genuinely fixed for the deterministic counters, and the residual judgment call is correctly isolated. The lesson is narrower than the change -- moving a check from a judge to a function silently redefines any keyword whose meaning depended on a reader that understands negation. Audit trail for the accuracy figures cited here: golden-set accuracy 89.7% (35/39) at HEAD 2c3eaa7, versus 87.2% (34/39) at iter-17. NOT claimed as an improvement: different runs, live LLM variance, no significance test, and the two runs do not share a dataset revision.
